subject: Food Science
title: Gelatin and Alternatives
description: A fast breakdown of Gelatin and Alternatives for builders.

hook.text: Jell-O jiggles because of collagen extracted from pig skin and cattle bones. Gelatin is an animal product.

buildup.text: Gelatin dissolves in warm water and sets into a gel when cooled. It's used in gummies, marshmallows, and yogurt.

discovery.text: Gelatin's triple-helix protein structure creates a thermoreversible gel—it melts on your tongue at body temperature.

twist.text: Gelatin excludes vegetarians, vegans, Jews, and Muslims from many foods. The search for replacements is huge.

climax.text: Agar from seaweed, pectin from fruit, and carrageenan from red algae are plant-based gelatin alternatives.

punchline.text: Your gummy bear is made from bones. The alternatives come from the sea.

quiz.question: What makes gelatin unique as a gelling agent?
options: It's thermoreversible—melting at body temperature on your tongue
